description:
FILED s400, from the #348 measurement.  NOT reachable on main today: s400
landed only the machine-portability half of #207 (which_perl returns $^X), so
this file still runs its children under real perl and still reads 16/6.  It is
one of the two holes holding #348.

WITH which_perl -> $PCLPERL (tools/pclperl-for-tests), run/cloexec.t goes
16/6 DIFF -> TIMEOUT with 2 rows.

WHAT IS KNOWN:
 * It emits rows 1-2 and then stops at row 3, which is the first
   test_not_inherited call -- i.e. the first `my $out = `$cmd`` with STDERR
   redirected to a temp file and *SAVERR holding a dup of the original.
 * It does not finish at --timeout 400 either (still 2 rows), so it is a HANG,
   not slowness.
 * The child program by itself does NOT hang.  Run directly,
     tools/pclperl-for-tests -e '<the $Child_prog one-liner>' 3
   returns rc=0 in about a second.  It does print something perl does not:
   perl dies `open 3: Bad file descriptor`, PCL opens fd 3 successfully and
   prints the TRANSPILED CL (";;; pcl: pipeline=v2 gen=...") -- fd 3 is OPEN in
   the PCL child and is not in a perl child, which is itself a finding about
   what pclperl-for-tests leaks to the program it runs.
 * A plain backtick capture of a pclperl-for-tests child does NOT hang
   (out=$(tools/pclperl-for-tests -e 'print qq{x\n}') returns), so the hang
   needs cloexec's fd / STDERR-redirect context.

SUSPECT (not measured): a grandchild inherits the backtick pipe's write end and
outlives the child, so the parent never sees EOF -- the #273 shape.  The cheap
discriminating measurement: run the file with the switch on, and when it
stalls, read /proc/<sbcl-pid>/fd and find which process still holds the pipe.

ALSO WORTH A LOOK while in there: pclperl-for-tests writes a long run of BLANK
LINES to stderr for a trivial program (visible in any terminal capture) -- the
stderr scrubber passes them through.  Harmless for row counts, noisy in logs.


ORDER (ruled s401): FIRST of the #348 pair â it is a bug in
tools/pclperl-for-tests on its own (fd 3 leaks into every child it runs;
the blank-line stderr noise), independent of which_perl.  Session C of
docs/plan-post-s400.md.


HARNESS HALF DONE s404 (commit df10b95) — both bugs the task named, each
measured:

  * fd LEAK: `load` held prog.lisp open while the program ran, so the child saw
    fd 3 AND fd 4 pointing at it and `open(my $t, "<&=3")` SUCCEEDED where perl
    fails EBADF.  Fixed by slurping the source, closing the file, then
    read+eval one form at a time from a string stream (incremental reads keep
    `(in-package …)` working — it is a READ-time effect).  Measured after: fds
    3 and 4 closed.
  * BLANK-LINE NOISE: 56 empty stderr lines for `print "hello\n"` — SBCL frames
    each compiler-note block with a blank line and the scrubber kept the
    frames.  Now dropped when adjacent to a scrubbed block, KEPT when the
    program printed them (`warn "first\n"; warn "\n"; warn "last\n"` is
    byte-identical to perl).

STILL OPEN (this is where the next session starts):
  1. The HANG itself is not re-measured with the fd fix in place.  The cheap
     way in needs NO code change: `$^X` honours the PERL env var, and
     which_perl returns `$^X`, so
         PERL=$PWD/tools/pclperl-for-tests tools/run-perl-suite.pl run/cloexec.t \
             --jobs 1 --timeout 300
     reproduces the #348 configuration for one file.  If it still stalls, the
     task's discriminating measurement stands: read /proc/<sbcl-pid>/fd at the
     stall and find who still holds the backtick pipe.
  2. The runners row of the WHAT-CHANGED table owes a companion re-run compared
     file-by-file, since tools/pclperl-for-tests changed.


CLOSED s405: the cause was #358 (open on a closed fd spun on EBADF), not the harness; run/cloexec.t TIMEOUT -> DIFF 16/6.
subject: run/cloexec.t HANGS at its first backtick child when which_perl points at the PCL child interpreter (measured s400; blocks #348)
